predictions.title: Agent-framework loaders ship signed-checkpoint and manifest mode by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the May 10 agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE pair forces open-source agent frameworks to ship signature-verified checkpoint deserialization plus signature-verified plugin-manifest fetching as the documented default loader mode across the AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, LangGraph, CrewAI, Haystack, and LiteLLM cohort. The catalysts that land in a single Sunday-evening Pacific cycle are concrete and mutually reinforcing: AutoGen CVE-2026-44612 (CVSS 8.9) is an arbitrary-code-execution checkpoint-deserialization vulnerability in the agent-state-replay path, exploitable through a malicious checkpoint uploaded via a connected message broker, patched same-day in AutoGen v0.5.18; Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-44638 (CVSS 8.4) is an authenticated server-side request forgery in the plugin-manifest fetcher allowing pivot to internal cloud-metadata endpoints, patched in Semantic Kernel v1.36.0 with an out-of-band dotnet packaging advisory; Trail of Bits publishes a joint Sunday write-up cataloging both as the same agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader exposure pattern previously documented in the May 8 CrewAI CVE-2026-44352 plus Haystack CVE-2026-44391 survey; the NHS England agentic-AI workflow-platform CVE blocklist already names LangGraph CVE-2026-44012, LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188, CrewAI CVE-2026-44352, and Haystack CVE-2026-44391 as disallowed pre-patch versions on NHS-tenant deployments, with the AutoGen plus Semantic Kernel pair expected to join inside the CISA May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline window. The structural force is that once Trail of Bits catalogs four-then-six CVEs across the open-source agent-framework cohort as one exposure class, framework maintainers can no longer ship checkpoint-deserialization and plugin-manifest-fetcher paths as opt-in trust surfaces; the security posture inverts from voluntary signature checking to signed-by-default with a deliberate opt-out for sandboxed test fixtures. The most likely shape is a signed-checkpoint primitive added as a first-class object across the framework cohort with deterministic Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature verification at load time plus a manifest-fetcher policy schema that allowlists URL prefixes and enforces a fetched-manifest signature chain anchored to the framework distribution. Sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt it first because the NHS England plus France DGFiP plus Germany Bundesagentur fuer Arbeit sovereign-cloud cohort treats per-CVE remediation status as paired procurement-eligibility evidence and the Anthropic per-tenant attestation log (arxiv 2605.05933 plus 2605.06012 compositional safety theorems) is becoming the canonical compliance shape. Bear case is a framework forking the loader contract and refusing the signature-verification default in favor of a sandbox-only mitigation; absent that, Q4 2026 lands signed-checkpoint and manifest mode as the documented default across the cohort.

reasoning.so_that: AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, LangGraph, CrewAI, Haystack, LiteLLM ship signature-verified loader as documented default.

reasoning.plain_language: Microsoft and rival open-source agent tools all got hit by the same loader bug, so they will require signed files by default.

predictions.summary: Microsoft AutoGen CVE-2026-44612 (CVSS 8.9 checkpoint deserialization RCE) and Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-44638 (CVSS 8.4 plugin-manifest SSRF) land Sunday following the May 8 CrewAI+Haystack agent-loader pattern. By Q4 2026 agent-framework loaders ship signed-checkpoint and manifest mode by default.

predictions.title: Capability-attestation rider lands as default defense-prime AI MSA by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the May 10 Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 day-three registry-telemetry consolidation — the per-tenant Mythos Preview gating contractual ethics-and-misuse rider crossing from the US-defense-industrial cohort (JPMorgan Chase, Booz Allen Hamilton, Mandiant Consulting, Raytheon, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Palo Alto Networks Unit 42) into the European NATO-allied defense-prime tier (BAE Systems UK, Rheinmetall AG Germany, Thales SA France) on Sunday, lifting the gated cohort to 44 enterprise tenants with 29 cumulative Mythos-class auto-quarantines (11 traced to original signatories) against 17,200 published skills and 1.46M day-three installs — combined with the May 9 arxiv 2605.05933 leakage-freedom proof for the gating composition rule co-authored by MIT CSAIL, ETH Zurich, and Anthropic, the May 10 arxiv 2605.06012 multi-tenant compositional safety theorem (adding Microsoft as co-author and enabling formal verification of sovereign-cloud plus FedRAMP-Moderate plus per-org-agent-registry deployment shapes), AWS Bedrock Agent Registry's pull-forward of OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise interop into FedRAMP-Moderate public preview ahead of the Q3 GA window, Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center's parallel public-preview interop with the Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 sandboxed-skill registry on composition rules, and Simon Willison's Sunday note documenting the per-tenant attestation-log audit-trail review as repeatable across all 44 gated tenants, force the per-tenant capability-attestation rider to harden from an Anthropic-specific contractual artifact into the default master-services-agreement addendum shape that NATO-allied defense primes, sovereign-cloud regulated tenants, and Indo-Pacific reciprocity-cohort enterprise buyers require as a standard procurement-eligibility clause for frontier-lab AI deployments. The forcing function is that once three European NATO-prime signatories adopt the rider inside a single weekend cycle and the leakage-freedom proof plus multi-tenant compositional safety theorem give corporate counsel a citable safety theorem rather than a hand-waved governance pattern, MSA negotiation cycles for the OpenAI per-org agent registry, Google DeepMind Gemini Enterprise, Mistral Workflows sovereign-cloud tenancy, and the three hyperscaler-managed registries cannot let attestation-log access, gating-composition-rule disclosure, and per-tenant Mythos-class quarantine evidence remain ad-hoc when the Anthropic shape has demonstrated audit-trail repeatability across 44 gated tenants with a published arxiv proof anchoring the no-cross-tenant-leakage claim. The most likely shape is a six-clause rider template (per-tenant capability-attestation log access, gating-composition-rule disclosure to the buyer's counsel, Mythos-class auto-quarantine evidence delivery cadence, sovereign-cloud execution-jurisdiction warranty mirroring the Mistral Workflows control-plane separation precedent, cyber-eval reciprocity-attestation field interop covering the six-jurisdiction Indo-Pacific cohort, and an ethics-and-misuse termination right) entering the model AI-procurement MSA templates of at least three Big-4 enterprise law firms (Latham, Wachtell, Kirkland, or Skadden) plus the GAO + UK Crown Commercial Service + EU Joint Procurement reference templates. NATO-allied defense primes and sovereign-cloud FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt first because their procurement frameworks already require both per-tenant capability-gating evidence and named-jurisdiction execution boundaries. Bear case is that hyperscaler-managed equivalents (Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog tenant-policy schema, AWS Bedrock Agent Registry FedRAMP inheritance, Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center attestation field) ship a parallel hyperscaler-mediated rider shape that frontier labs route through rather than negotiate bilaterally; absent that, Q4 2026 lands the capability-attestation rider as the default defense-prime AI MSA addendum across the cohort.

predictions.title: CISA pairs agentic-AI CVE remediation with capability attestation by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the agentic-AI workflow-platform CVE wave converging across the May 8 to May 11 window forces CISA to publish a Binding Operational Directive that treats per-CVE remediation status and per-tenant Mythos-class capability attestation logs as paired federal-civilian-executive-branch procurement and operating requirements, with the operative review cadence pegged to the May 21 n8n CVE-2026-21858 federal-civilian remediation deadline. The catalysts landing in a single news cycle are concrete and mutually reinforcing: the AutoGen CVE-2026-44612 checkpoint-deserialization remote-code-execution path plus the Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-44638 plugin-manifest authenticated server-side request forgery to internal cloud-metadata endpoints extend the May 8 CrewAI plus Haystack and the earlier LangGraph plus LiteLLM CVE cluster across the full Microsoft open-source agent stack inside one weekend, with Trail of Bits cataloging the shared agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader exposure pattern; CISA's Sunday-edition KEV catalog note expressly reminds federal-civilian-executive-branch agencies of the May 21 n8n remediation deadline while the agentic-AI CVE wave compounds on top; the Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center director plus the NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director joining the May 15 S-407 classified Frontier Model Review Board threshold briefing carries the operational view of Mythos-class capability exposure on enterprise tenants directly into the executive-order interagency-review conversation; the Sunday three-hyperscaler registry interop matrix (AWS Bedrock public-preview FedRAMP-Moderate pull-forward, Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center adding Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 sandboxed-skill registry interop, and the Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog mirroring the South Korea PIPC plus New Zealand GCSB cyber-eval reciprocity attestation fields in the tenant-policy schema alongside the May 8 Singapore IMDA plus Japan AISI integration) demonstrates that the cross-vendor compliance plumbing already exists across all six Indo-Pacific reciprocity-cohort jurisdictions; the May 9 arxiv 2605.05933 leakage-freedom proof for per-tenant capability attestation plus the May 10 arxiv 2605.06012 multi-tenant compositional safety theorem give the directive drafters a citable formal-verification anchor; and the NHS England agentic-AI workflow-platform CVE blocklist (Ni8mare plus LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 plus LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188 plus CrewAI CVE-2026-44352 plus Haystack CVE-2026-44391, now with AutoGen and Semantic Kernel as obvious additions) already demonstrates the publishable per-CVE blocklist shape that an allied public-sector procurement regime can pair with the attestation-log evidence requirement. The structural force is that the May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline arrives before the May 22 earliest FMRB executive-order signing window, leaving CISA as the operative federal-civilian-executive-branch enforcement vehicle while the policy regime is still in interagency review; the agency cannot let the AutoGen plus Semantic Kernel disclosure pattern sit as a coincidence after publishing four prior agentic-platform KEV additions in three weeks. The most likely shape is a Binding Operational Directive scoping agentic-AI workflow platforms (named explicitly to include n8n, LangGraph, LiteLLM, CrewAI, Haystack, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel) with a paired requirement: per-CVE remediation status plus per-tenant Mythos-class capability attestation log evidence (the Anthropic Project Glasswing primitive plus the formal-verification framework from the arxiv 2605.05933 plus 2605.06012 papers as the cited compliance evidence) on a federal-civilian estate, with the review cadence aligned to the n8n CVE-2026-21858 May 21 deadline. Sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate tenants comply first because the AWS Bedrock plus Google Cloud Vertex public-preview interop matrix already exposes the attestation-log field. Bear case is that the FMRB executive order ships first with the agentic-AI workflow scope pre-empted; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the directive across the federal-civilian-executive-branch perimeter.
